method: OPEN AND QUOTED from Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021' (published 2022). Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: CC BY (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC9269181).

claims.claim: **Suspect Fabry disease** with typical features (acroparesthesias, angiokeratomas, hypohidrosis, cornea verticillata) and a family history.
claims.source_text: Individuals showing previously described signs and symptoms and a family history of the condition should be suspected for Fabry disease.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm in males by α-Gal A enzyme activity** (classic disease: under 5% or absent) plus a disease-causing GLA variant. **In females enzyme activity may be normal**, so genetic testing is key; plasma lyso-GL3 helps in doubtful cases.
claims.source_text: Males with classic variants have very low (< 5%) or absent enzyme activity levels, while late-onset cases present variable enzyme activity levels (5-30%). … Symptomatic females with FD may present normal to slightly diminished enzyme activity levels, and such finding does not rule out a diagnosis of FD. … Genetic testing is of paramount importance in the definitive diagnosis of female patients … Plasma lyso-GL3 is more sensitive and specific for patients of either of the sexes, correlates with FD phenotype, and may be elevated in females with normal enzyme activity.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen at-risk groups:** unexplained proteinuria or albuminuria, dialysis (CKD 5D), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, or stroke/TIA without another cause. After an index case, build a pedigree of at least three generations and test every relative.
claims.source_text: Screening for FD is recommended for patients categorized as belonging to populations at risk of disease, a group that includes subjects with kidney disorders such as proteinuria or albuminuria, individuals with stage 5D CKD, heart disease such as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, or cerebrovascular disease such as stroke or TIA not explained by other causes. … After an index case has been found, building a pedigree covering at least three generations and investigating every family member - even asymptomatic ones - for X-linked inheritance pattern is recommended.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classic disease (males and females): treat as soon as there are early signs of Fabry-related organ involvement.** (Class I) ERT should be offered to classic males from age seven even without symptoms. (Class IIa)
claims.source_text: Males and females with classic phenotype disease must be treated as soon as early signs of FD-related target organ involvement are present (CLASS I RECOMMENDATION). … we recommend that ERT should be offered to males with classic FD from the age of seven years, even in the absence of signs or symptoms (CLASS IIA RECOMMENDATION).
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptomatic females: always treat. Asymptomatic females: treat if there is kidney injury** (GFR below 90 mL/min/1.73m², albumin-to-creatinine ratio persistently above 30 mg/g, or biopsy changes).
claims.source_text: Symptomatic females: Always initiate specific treatment. … Asymptomatic females: Start specific therapy if there is workup or histology evidence of kidney injury, such as a GFR of less than 90 mL/min/1.73m, an ARC persistently greater than 30 mg/g, or foot process effacement, moderate or severe GL3 inclusions and signs of glomerulosclerosis in kidney tissue.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Kidney criteria in males:** treat albuminuria/proteinuria (ACR above 30 mg/g) and/or mild-to-moderate Fabry CKD (GFR above 60). (Class I) Podocyte GL3 deposits on biopsy are an indication even without proteinuria. (Class I)
claims.source_text: treatment is indicated for males with urinary protein and/or proteinuria (ARC greater than 30 mg/g) and/or mild to moderate CKD (GFR greater than 60 mL/min/1.73m) related to FD (CLASS I RECOMMENDATION). … The presence of FD-related histology alterations such as GL3 deposits in podocyte cells amount to treatment indication, even in the absence of clinical signs of kidney involvement such as proteinuria/microalbuminuria (CLASS I RECOMMENDATION).
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Variant of uncertain significance:** treat adults with biochemical or biopsy evidence of Fabry kidney involvement. (Class IIb) **Over 50 years:** age alone does not rule treatment out; decide individually.
claims.source_text: Adult male or female subjects with VUS must be treated when there is biochemical or histology evidence of FD-related kidney involvement, even if other symptoms are absent (CLASSE IIB RECOMMENDATION). … Patients aged 50+ years do not have a clear-cut indication about when to initiate treatment. If analyzed in isolation, being older than 50 years is not a contraindication in itself
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Patients who do not meet criteria yet** need periodic review for organ involvement and treatment once it appears.
claims.source_text: Patients failing to meet the criteria for therapy upon diagnosis must be monitored periodically for FD-related organ involvement and have therapy initiated as soon as it becomes needed.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Migalastat (oral chaperone) is only for amenable missense variants**, from age 16 years with GFR above 30 mL/min/1.73m²; it crosses the blood-brain barrier. With an amenable variant, choose between ERT and migalastat with the patient.
claims.source_text: This medication is indicated only to patients with amenable variants (susceptible to the drug) of the missense type. … Unlike ERT, migalastat crosses the blood-brain barrier. … It is important to mention that in the cases of patients with amenable variants it is up to the physician jointly with the patient to assess the favorable points of each therapy while deciding between ERT and chaperones. ERT with agalsidase alfa or beta has been approved for use in individuals aged seven or older and eight or older, respectively, while migalastat can be prescribed to patients aged 16 years or older with a GFR greater than 30 mL/min/1.73m.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Agalsidase ERT is given IV every 15 days** (alfa 0.2 mg/kg, beta 1 mg/kg; beta always needs premedication). Watch for infusion reactions and anti-drug antibodies.
claims.source_text: The two drugs are administered intravenously every 15 days, since the enzymes in question are rapidly depleted in plasma. The recommended doses for agalsidase alfa and beta are 0.2 mg/kg/dose and 1 mg/kg/dose, respectively. Differently from agalsidase alfa, agalsidase beta always requires pre-medication. … One of the main adverse events is infusion reaction characterized by fever, rigors, edema, skin rash, nausea, dyspnea, and development of anti-agalsidase antibodies.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not start therapy** in CKD 4–5 not eligible for transplant with NYHA IV heart failure, or with advanced disease and life expectancy under a year. IgE antibodies to agalsidase are generally an absolute contraindication.
claims.source_text: Treatment is not recommended for patients with CKD stages 4 or 5 ineligible for kidney transplantation with NYHA class IV HF or any advanced disease leading to a life expectancy of less than a year. … The presence of anti-IgE antibodies against agalsidase is generally considered an absolute contraindication given the risk of anaphylactic reaction.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pregnancy:** a relative contraindication for ERT; migalastat is contraindicated. Advise women to stop before conceiving and while breastfeeding, and to use contraception.
claims.source_text: Pregnancy is a relative contraindication for ERT. … Migalastat is contraindicated during pregnancy for lack of safety data. Females must be advised to discontinue therapy before conceiving and while they are breastfeeding, and to use contraceptives.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stop or change therapy for poor adherence (missing over 50% of infusions), loss to follow-up, unwillingness, or severe ERT reactions.** (Class I)
claims.source_text: Poor compliance (patients missing more than 50% of infusion sessions), patients lost during follow-up, and patients unwilling to be treated rank among the top indications to suspend therapy. Patients meeting contraindication criteria (Table 7) during treatment must be assessed for therapy discontinuation. In this consensus document, the presence of severe reactions to ERT was deemed as an indication to discontinue therapy (CLASS I RECOMMENDATION) or change medication.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow CKD guidelines, with ACE inhibitor or ARB for proteinuria;** blood pressure target 130/80 mmHg or lower.
claims.source_text: In cases of FD nephropathy, the guidelines for the treatment of CKD must be followed, including measures to control systemic hypertension and promote smoking cessation, along with individualized diets and dyslipidemia therapy. … Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) blockade using angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) is an important measure, since these drugs decrease proteinuria and offer cardioprotection. Table 8 describes therapeutic goals. Blood pressure (BP) targets are as follows: Systolic BP ≤ 130 mmHg and diastolic BP ≤ 80 mmHg.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Kidney goal on therapy:** GFR decline under 3 mL/min/1.73m²/year.
claims.source_text: The goal is to reduce the annual GFR decline to values less than 3 mL/min/1.73m2/year.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor GFR and albuminuria/proteinuria** at least yearly at low risk, six-monthly at moderate risk and three-monthly at high risk, whether or not on therapy.
claims.source_text: Care to patients with FD must be based on early assessment and regular functional monitoring of potentially affected organs to check for disease progression, regardless of whether patients are on specific therapy. … Ideal kidney monitoring includes the analysis of the GFR and albuminuria/proteinuria at least annually in patients at low risk of developing CKD, every six months if risk is rated as moderate, and every three months for high-risk patients.
claims.locator: Committee for Rare Diseases (Comdora), Brazilian Society of Nephrology, Jornal Brasileiro de Nefrologia, 'Brazilian consensus recommendations for the diagnosis, screening, and treatment of individuals with fabry disease: Committee for Rare Diseases - Brazilian Society of Nephrology/2021', published 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9269181/, retrieved 2026-09-23
